I will keep to a simple, low-risk plan that fits Quzhou County and the start of the season. I will plant my usual grain system, with winter wheat already in the ground from last autumn and summer maize after wheat harvest, because that is the most dependable way for me to use the land, spread labor across the year, and secure both yield and cash. I will not make the plan too complicated. At my age, I would rather choose crops I know, use improved or hybrid seed where it gives stable yield, and manage fertilizer, water, and spraying carefully instead of chasing a risky high-input crop. For wheat, I will focus on topdressing nitrogen at jointing, one or two irrigations if water is available, and disease control if I see pressure. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, apply enough base fertilizer, irrigate at key growth stages if needed, and spray only when pests or weeds justify it. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is practical and saves labor. My goal is stable production, manageable fieldwork, and lower risk rather than trying something unfamiliar.
